source.check: returned unopposed: no contest for the County Council and this division not among the changes (Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5; Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1936, p. 9); present at the first meeting of the new council, Monday 15 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 20 June 1936, p. 3)

note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1936. Nominations were lodged on 5 May; 'There are no contests for the County Council. The 27 electoral areas will be represented in the new Council by 16 Unionists and 11 Nationalists' (Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5), and the Belfast News-Letter of 6 May 1936, p. 9 names the only changes in personnel: Coagh, Donaghmore, Killeter, Pomeroy and Trillick; no nomination was received for Dromore, whose member was deemed re-elected. The unchanged divisions are recorded by the meeting method (7 Nov 2026): each member is the 1933 return for the division (Mid-Ulster Mail, 22 April 1933, p. 6), or, for Ballygawley and Newtownstewart, the member co-opted in 1934 after a death, and each sat on the new council in 1936 (first meeting of Monday 15 June 1936, Ulster Herald, 20 June 1936, p. 3; later meetings of August and September 1936). Omagh Urban is not recorded: its outgoing member was Mr. A. E. Donnelly, M.P., co-opted in May 1935 on the death of Mr. Michael Lynch (Ulster Herald, 1 June 1935, p. 10), but no 1936 report read places him on the new council. The polling day for Tyrone was Wednesday 3 June 1936; there was no county council contest. Filed on 1936-06-03, the Tyrone polling day (previously filed under 1936-05-28, 6 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 31 May 1933 return (John Glasgow (deemed re-elected 1933); Mid-Ulster Mail, 22 April 1933, p. 6); the Ulster Herald, 20 June 1936, p. 3 names the member as returned, sitting on the new council. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
